translationRepairs: Liu Hong, General Who Guards the South and Zhan’s grandfather on his mother’s side, invited him as senior clerk and told him, “Your talent and judgment run deep; in time you will succeed me in holding the Jing southlands.”

Liu Hong, General Who Guards the South and the brother of Zhan’s grandmother, invited him as senior clerk and told him, “Your talent and judgment run deep; in time you will succeed me in holding the Jing southlands.”
祖舅 means the brother of one's grandmother (a great-uncle), not a maternal grandfather; literal error: "grandfather on his mother's side".
He also received the title of cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and eventually became minister of the imperial clan.
He also received the title of cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and eventually became Superintendent of the Palace.
光祿勳 is the Superintendent of the Palace (Guanglu xun), not the minister of the imperial clan (宗正); literal error: office mistranslated.
The court issued a patent posthumously naming him General Who Guards the South with three-offices protocol, styled him “Stalwart,” and offered him the great beast sacrifice.
The court issued a patent posthumously naming him General-in-Chief Who Guards the South with three-offices protocol, styled him “Stalwart,” and offered him the great beast sacrifice.
鎮南大將軍 includes 大 (General-in-Chief); literal error: the translation drops "-in-Chief" from the posthumous office.
His brother Ying Dan was capable and forceful, served as magistrate over six commanderies and as General Who Inspires Might, and was posthumously named inspector of Ji.
His brother Ying Dan was capable and forceful, served as magistrate over six commanderies and as General of the Soaring Dragon, and was posthumously named inspector of Ji.
龍驤將軍 means General of the Soaring Dragon; literal error: rendered as "General Who Inspires Might", which is a different title.
His father Gan Chang was junior tutor to the heir apparent.
His father Gan Chang was Grand Tutor to the heir apparent.
太子太傅 is the Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; literal error: "junior tutor" would be 少傅.
He eventually became junior minister of the palace.
He eventually became Chamberlain of the Lesser Treasury.
少府卿 is the Chamberlain of the Lesser Treasury (Shaofu); literal error: "junior minister of the palace" mistranslates the office.
Zhuo was soon raised to General Who Pacifies the South, inspector of Liang, with staff of authority over the forces north of the Han, based at Xiangyang.
Zhuo was soon raised to General Who Calms the South, inspector of Liang, with staff of authority over the forces north of the Han, based at Xiangyang.
安南將軍 is General Who Calms the South; literal error: rendered with the name of a different title, 平南 (Pacifies the South).
During Taining he was posthumously named General Who Inspires Might with the style “Reverent.”
During Taining he was posthumously named General of Agile Cavalry with the style “Reverent.”
驃騎將軍 is the General of Agile Cavalry; literal error: rendered as "General Who Inspires Might".

Imperial orders raised Zhuo to General Who Guards the South, palace attendant, area commander for Jing and Liang, and shepherd of Jing while he kept Liang inspector; Tao Kan, reading Zhuo’s letter, immediately sent Gao Bao downriver with troops.

Imperial orders raised Zhuo to General-in-Chief Who Guards the South, palace attendant, area commander for Jing and Liang, and shepherd of Jing while he kept Liang inspector; Tao Kan, reading Zhuo’s letter, immediately sent Gao Bao downriver with troops.
鎮南大將軍 includes 大 (General-in-Chief); literal error: the "-in-Chief" grade is dropped.
By then the imperial army had lost; Wang Dun demanded a palace escort with the Yu banner to stop Gan Zhuo.
By then the imperial army had lost; Wang Dun requested the court's Zouyu banner to halt Gan Zhuo.
騶虞幡 is the Zouyu banner used to order a halt to hostilities; literal error: "a palace escort with the Yu banner" misreads 騶虞 as an escort plus a name.
His four sons, Fan and the rest, all died with him.
His four sons, including the cavalier gentleman Fan, were all killed.
散騎郎蕃 gives Fan's office (cavalier gentleman), which the translation omits; literal error: office dropped.
After Yang Jun fell, Cui vaulted to right secretariat aide, village marquis of Chengyang, and eventually General of the Right Army.
After Yang Jun fell, Cui vaulted to right secretariat aide, viscount of Chengyang, and eventually General of the Right Army.
封成陽子 is enfeoffment as a viscount (子) of Chengyang; literal error: "village marquis" misstates the rank.
When Jiyin fell he fled east to his brother-in-law Pei Dun, inspector of Xu province.
When his home province fell he fled east to his brother-in-law Pei Dun, inspector of Xu province.
本州 means his home province (Yanzhou), not Jiyin commandery; literal error: the place is over-specified as Jiyin.
He rose to mentor to the heir apparent, then was dismissed over a bureaucratic affair.
He rose to supervisor of the heir apparent’s household, then was dismissed over a bureaucratic affair.
太子詹事 is the Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent; literal error: "mentor to the heir apparent" misnames the office.
Zu Xian, Situ and duke of Linying, should spread the five bonds yet swallowed this breach without demotion;
Zu, Palace Attendant, Minister over the Masses and Duke of Linying, whose charge is to spread the five teachings, yet swallowed this breach without demotion;
組 is the given name of Xun Zu; 敷宣 means "spread", not part of a name. Literal error: "Zu Xian" invents a name and drops the office 侍中.
At Cheng’s accession the ministers brought the jade seal; Wang Dao, claiming illness, stayed away.
When Emperor Ming died and Emperor Cheng took the throne, the ministers brought the jade seal; Wang Dao, claiming illness, stayed away.
帝崩，成帝即位 states Emperor Ming's death before Emperor Cheng's accession; literal error: the death is omitted.
Wang Dao read the debate and raised the award to General Who Inspires Might with palace attendant.
Wang Dao read the debate and raised the award to General of Agile Cavalry with palace attendant.
驃騎將軍 is the General of Agile Cavalry; literal error: rendered as "General Who Inspires Might".
The court reissued patent: palace attendant, General Who Inspires Might, three-offices mansion, styled “Loyal and True,” with the great sacrifice.
The court reissued patent: palace attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, three-offices mansion, styled “Loyal and True,” with the great sacrifice.
驃騎將軍 is the General of Agile Cavalry; literal error: rendered as "General Who Inspires Might".
As Wang Mi threatened Luoyang, Dun and Hu Wuzhi begged Sima Yue to attack; Wang Yan and Pan Tao blocked the plan while Dun shouted himself hoarse in open court—the crowd admired his nerve.
As Wang Mi threatened Luoyang, Dun and Huwu Fuzhi begged Sima Yue to attack; Wang Yan and Pan Tao blocked the plan while Dun shouted himself hoarse in open court—the crowd admired his nerve.
胡毋輔之 is Huwu Fuzhi (double surname Huwu, given name Fuzhi); literal error: "Hu Wuzhi" splits the surname and drops 輔.
He moved to minister of the imperial clan, then area commander as General Who Pacifies the South and Xiang inspector with staff.
He moved to Superintendent of the Palace, then area commander as General Who Calms the South and Xiang inspector with staff.
光祿勳 is the Superintendent of the Palace and 安南將軍 is General Who Calms the South; literal errors: "minister of the imperial clan" and "Pacifies the South".
Wang Dao, favoring mercy after the chaos, banished him to Guang as General Who Pacifies the South instead.
Wang Dao, favoring mercy after the chaos, banished him to Guang as General Who Calms the South instead.
安南將軍 is General Who Calms the South; literal error: rendered with the title 平南 (Pacifies the South).
After the victory he was posthumously named minister of the imperial clan.
After the victory he was posthumously named Superintendent of the Palace.
光祿勳 is the Superintendent of the Palace; literal error: "minister of the imperial clan" is a different office (宗正).
Peace made him General Who Dashes the Enemy.
Peace made him General of Valiant Cavalry.
驍騎將軍 is the General of Valiant Cavalry; literal error: rendered as "General Who Dashes the Enemy".
When Liu Xia’s bodyguard mutinied, Guo Mo marched under Zhong Ya’s staff command.
When Liu Xia, General of the Northern Gentlemen, died and his retainers mutinied, Guo Mo was ordered to suppress them, with Zhong Ya supervising the campaign and holding the staff of authority.
劉遐卒…以雅監征討軍事、假節: the translation omits Liu Xia's death and office and misstates Zhong Ya's role; literal error: Guo Mo did not serve under a "staff command".
